title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 5th District
area: North and central Louisiana, including the Delta and Avoyelles, Rapides and Ouachita parishes.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026. If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map. This is an open seat: incumbent Julia Letlow (R) did not seek re-election here, running instead for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Michael Echols
candidates.currentRole: Louisiana State Representative, District 14 (Chairman, House Republican Delegation)

summary.text: Michael Echols is a Republican state representative from Monroe who has served in the Louisiana House since 2020, after a term on the Monroe City Council. He works in business and real-estate development and, according to Ballotpedia, became the House Republican caucus's majority leader in December 2025. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he is running on public safety, an economy built around domestic production, and reducing federal spending.

background.text: Born in Bastrop, Louisiana, in 1977; lives in Monroe, where, according to his campaign materials, he lives with his wife Christie and their two daughters.
Graduated from Prairie View Academy; earned a B.A. in accounting (1999) and an M.B.A. (2001) from the University of Louisiana at Monroe.

Early career: chief operations officer of Oglesby Financial Group (2000-2007) and associate vice president of marketing and communication at the University of Louisiana at Monroe (2007-2010); later director of business development for Vantage Health Plan.

Describes himself as leading Echo Development, a real-estate development company that has revitalized historic properties across North Louisiana, including The Hotel Monroe, and as host of the long-running radio show "Echols at 8."
Was a Republican candidate for Louisiana House District 14 in 2011.
Elected to the Monroe City Council (District 1) in 2016 and served as council chair from 2016 to 2017.
Elected to the Louisiana House of Representatives, District 14, taking office on January 13, 2020; re-elected in 2023.

Committee assignments in the 2025-2026 term include Ways and Means, Health and Welfare, Labor and Industrial Relations, the Joint Capital Outlay Committee and the Medicaid Oversight Committee; he began serving as House Majority Leader on December 11, 2025, according to Ballotpedia.

In 2024, testified before the U.S. Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions about Steward Health Care's management of Glenwood Regional Medical Center in West Monroe, according to Wikipedia.

priorities.text: Says Washington has failed on public safety and pledges to use federal tools to put more officers on the street and target repeat violent offenders.
priorities.quote: Washington has failed on public safety. I'll use federal tools to put more officers on the street, support law enforcement, and go after repeat violent offenders. Safe communities come first.

priorities.text: Wants to cut regulation and expand energy production, including oil and gas and data infrastructure along the I-20 corridor.
priorities.quote: Cut red tape, unleash energy, and bring jobs back home. From oil and gas to new data infrastructure along I-20, we should be leading—not watching opportunity leave.

priorities.text: Pledges to rein in federal spending, saying Washington "spends too much, wastes too much, and puts Americans last."

positions.summary: Pledges to use federal tools to put more officers on the street and support law enforcement.
positions.quote: I'll use federal tools to put more officers on the street, support law enforcement, and go after repeat violent offenders.

record.text: Serves as Louisiana State Representative for District 14 and Chairman of the House Republican Delegation.

summary.text: Misti Cordell is a Monroe Republican who chairs the Louisiana Board of Regents, the board that coordinates public higher education in the state. She previously worked in health care recruiting and as an outreach representative in the Louisiana Attorney General's office. The Louisiana Republican Party endorsed her in this race in late August 2026, and she describes herself as the only political outsider in the field.

background.text: Graduated from Louisiana Tech University with a bachelor's degree in human resource management; lives in Monroe, according to the Board of Regents.
Works as a physician recruiter for Affinity Health Group in Monroe, according to the Board of Regents' 2024 announcement.
Served on Gov. Jeff Landry's Health and Hospitals Transition Team and as an outreach representative for the Louisiana Attorney General's Office.
Sworn in as an at-large member of the Louisiana Board of Regents on March 27, 2024 (term expires December 31, 2029); appointed chair by the governor in September 2024.
Serves or has served on the boards of MedCamps of Louisiana, the CenturyNext Bank advisory board, the Ouachita Parish Library and the Northeast Louisiana Children's Museum.

Received the Louisiana Republican Party's endorsement for this race at the end of August 2026; some opponents criticized the process, and Cordell described the endorsement as the product of her own outreach to State Central Committee members.

summary.text: Gabe Firment is a Republican state representative who has represented Louisiana House District 22 since 2020 and has chaired the House Insurance Committee in the 2025-2026 term. He has worked in the construction and insurance industries. He is one of three sitting state legislators running in the Republican field for this open seat.

background.text: Born around 1970 or 1971 and graduated from Tioga High School in 1989.
Earned a B.S. in public administration from Louisiana College (1994) and an M.B.A. from Louisiana Tech University.
Outside politics, has worked in the construction and insurance industries.
Elected to the Louisiana House of Representatives, District 22, in November 2019 and took office on January 13, 2020, succeeding Terry Brown; he was re-elected without opposition in 2023.
Has served on the House Insurance, Retirement, and Transportation, Highways and Public Works committees, and was assigned to chair the House Insurance Committee in 2025-2026.

record.text: Serving as Louisiana State Representative for District 22 since 2020.

summary.text: Stewart Cathey Jr. is a Republican state senator from the Monroe area, a business owner and a former Army engineer officer. He lost a 2015 state Senate race, won the District 33 seat in 2019, and now chairs the Senate Agriculture committee. He launched his congressional campaign in July 2026.

background.text: Born April 19, 1981.
Graduated from the University of Louisiana at Monroe.
Joined the U.S. Army in 2003 and served as a commissioned officer and Army engineer; deployed a second time in 2016.
Has worked as a managing partner at the Cathey Group since 2013.
Ran for Louisiana Senate District 35 in 2015 and lost to fellow Republican James Fannin.
Won Louisiana Senate District 33 in 2019, defeating Republican Wade Bishop with 52% of the vote, and took office in January 2020.

Committee assignments for 2025-2026 include chair of the Agriculture, Forestry, Aquaculture, and Rural Development Committee, along with Commerce, Consumer Protection, and International Affairs; Local and Municipal Affairs; and Technology and Cybersecurity.

record.text: Serving as Louisiana State Senator for District 33 since 2020.

summary.text: Oscar Dantzler, also listed as Omar, is a Republican candidate who has run for office several times before, including as a Democrat for this same congressional seat in 2022. No campaign website or biographical statement was found.

background.text: Ran as a candidate for Louisiana governor in 2019, receiving 0.8% of the vote as a Democrat.
Ran as a Democrat in the 2022 primary for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District, finishing second with 15.7% of the vote behind Rep. Julia Letlow.
Was listed as a Democratic candidate in the 2023 Louisiana governor's race but was among the withdrawn or disqualified candidates.

summary.text: Austin Magee describes himself as a blue-collar small business owner and builder with no previous political experience. He is running as a Republican on political reform, fiscal responsibility and oversight of artificial intelligence.

background.text: Describes himself as a blue-collar small business owner, builder and fixer.
Has no previous political experience and says he wants to prove an ordinary person can do the job.
background.quote: I want to prove that an ordinary person with no previous political experience can do the job with common sense and integrity.

background.text: Campaigns on banning congressional stock trading, a term-limits amendment, limits on lobbying and greater financial disclosure by politicians.

priorities.text: Wants to "reform politics itself," including banning congressional stock trading, passing a term-limits amendment, and limiting lobbying.
Calls for fiscal responsibility, saying the country cannot let politicians bankrupt it.
Wants federal action to regulate AI, saying it should never be given power to decide life or death.

positions.summary: Describes himself as "pro life" in his survey response.
Says he is passionate about protecting constitutional rights, especially the first and second amendments.
Says he supports law enforcement, the military and veterans.

candidates.name: Dan McKay
candidates.currentRole: Attorney; city attorney for Bunkie, Hessmer and Evergreen, Louisiana

summary.text: Dan McKay is a Democrat and attorney from Bunkie in Avoyelles Parish who has practiced law there for more than 45 years, including as a public defender, assistant district attorney and city attorney for several towns. He is a U.S. Army veteran. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he is running on protecting democratic principles, rural health care and reproductive health decisions.

background.text: Born in Monroe and raised in Mangham, Richland Parish, graduating from Mangham High School; says he has lived in the 5th District nearly all his life.
Holds bachelor's degrees from the University of Texas and the University of Louisiana at Monroe and a law degree from the LSU Law Center.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1970 to 1973, including two years overseas, and later commanded an Army Reserve unit in Baton Rouge while in law school.
Worked in broadcasting, construction and the offshore oilfield between his active Army service and his law practice.
Has maintained a general law practice in Avoyelles Parish for over 45 years, including 15 years as a public defender and more than 11 years as an assistant district attorney.
Has served as city attorney for Bunkie (12 years), Hessmer (24 years) and Evergreen (18 years).
Has been a member of the Bunkie Rotary Club for over 40 years, serving twice as president; says he is married with three children and six grandchildren.

priorities.text: Warns that about 20 rural hospitals in the 5th District are under threat of closing due to Medicaid cuts in the 2026 federal budget law.
Says healthcare should be viewed as a human right, and that a woman's healthcare decisions should be made between her and her medical professionals.
priorities.quote: Women's healthcare should be a matter of decision-making between a woman and her medical professionals.

priorities.text: Says the principles of democracy, including separation of church and state, free elections, rule of law, and a free press, are under attack and must be protected.

positions.summary: Says decisions about women's healthcare should be made between a woman and her medical professionals.
positions.quote: Women's healthcare should be a matter of decision-making between a woman and her medical professionals.

positions.summary: Says healthcare should be viewed as a human right and opposes Medicaid cuts that threaten rural hospitals in the district.
Says working people are "starved financially and paid sparsely while repeated tax cuts favor only the most wealthy."

summary.text: Pat Moore is a Democratic state representative from Monroe who has represented Louisiana House District 17 since 2019. A retired State Farm employee, she served on the Ouachita Parish Police Jury before joining the Legislature. She says she is running on protecting Medicaid, Medicare and Social Security and on her record of bills that became law.

background.text: Grew up in Monroe and graduated from Wossman High School.
Graduated from the College of Business at Northeast Louisiana University (now the University of Louisiana at Monroe).
Built a career with State Farm, from which she is retired.
Served on the Ouachita Parish Police Jury, representing District F, from 2007 to 2019.
Elected to the Louisiana House of Representatives, District 17, in 2019.
Committee assignments for 2025-2026 include Administration of Criminal Justice; Municipal, Parochial and Cultural Affairs; and Transportation, Highways and Public Works.

According to her survey, eight bills she wrote have become law, including protections for seniors buying Medicare supplement coverage and the law creating Louisiana's Community Health Worker Workforce Board.

summary.text: Antonio Wilson is a Democrat from Madison Parish who describes himself as a businessman, builder, father and community leader. He holds an MBA and has pursued doctoral-level graduate study, according to his Ballotpedia biography. He is running on economic development, infrastructure and investment in people.

background.text: Describes himself as a product of Madison Parish who completed his schooling in the Madison Parish school system.
According to his Ballotpedia biography, pursued undergraduate studies, earned an MBA and continued graduate education through the doctoral level.
Describes himself as a business owner and general contractor.

researchNotes: This is a crowded open-seat race (9 candidates). Michael Echols, Austin Magee, Dan McKay and Pat Moore completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, and Antonio Wilson has a candidate-submitted Ballotpedia biography. Misti Cordell, Oscar Dantzler and Antonio Wilson had no campaign website found. Gabe Firment and Stewart Cathey are current Louisiana state legislators but did not complete the survey or have an accessible campaign site with issue positions, so their biographies rely on Ballotpedia and Wikipedia. Biographical detail for Oscar Dantzler is limited to his prior election results.
